Interface OidcClaimsSource

public interface OidcClaimsSource
Supplies the standard claims an OpenID Provider asserts about one end user.

The seam between a provider endpoint and whatever holds identity data. A deployment implements this over its own directory, database, or attribute service; the endpoint asks it for a principal and never learns where the answer came from. That keeps an identity service free of OpenID Connect — it neither verifies tokens nor knows which relying party is asking — while the provider keeps the parts that are its own: which claims a grant's scope admits, whether what came back is who was asked about, and how what it publishes is signed and encrypted.

Who decides what is withheld

Not this. A provider works out which claims a grant's scope admits — from the sets OpenID Connect defines, deny-by-default — and names them. An implementation answers those and no others, and never has to reason about scope or about which relying party is asking. A source that holds more than was named simply doesn't volunteer it.

  • Method Details

    • claims

      edu.iu.oidc.IuOidcClaims claims(String principalName, Set<String> admittedClaims)
      Gets the claims this source holds for one principal, limited to those the provider named.

      The answer is what a provider publishes, so toString() must render it as the claims document a UserInfo response carries — a deployment configures that rendering for itself, and the provider signs and encrypts the result without looking at it.

      sub must answer principalName back. A relying party matches it against the ID token it holds and refuses the response when the two disagree, so a source that resolves a principal name to some other form — a username for a numeric ID, say — would break that comparison. A provider checks rather than trusting, and refuses to publish claims about anyone else.

      Parameters:
      principalName - principal name, which the provider has already settled from a verified grant, and which is also the sub the answer must carry
      admittedClaims - names of the claims the grant admits, sub among them; anything else this source holds is not to be answered
      Returns:
      claims held for principalName, limited to admittedClaims, rendering as a claims document
